What to do when a reply is cut off part-way. \"Send continue\" keeps what was written and asks the model to carry on. \"Regenerate last output\" throws away the broken part and re-sends the same request, so only that last stretch is redone — the rest of the conversation is untouched. Only active when auto-continue is on. Note: when the reply hits the output-length cap, \"send continue\" is always used, because regenerating would just hit the same cap again.

When the model a subagent is using crashes, times out or gets rate limited, it automatically retries with these models in order. Without fallback models the only safety net is your main chat model - and if the subagent already uses that model, there is no safety net at all.

Shown for the default role. If a role has its own model, that model replaces the first step for that role; the rest of the order stays the same.

If a subagent produces nothing new for this long, it is treated as stuck and that attempt is stopped, then the normal retry and model fallback path applies. Only idle time counts: a subagent that keeps producing output is never cut off by total runtime. Tool execution time is excluded and handled by "Tool time limit" below. Set to 0 to use the default of 10 minutes.

How long a single tool call (read file, search, web lookup) may run. Tools execute one at a time and produce no output while running, so this time does NOT count as idle and is governed here instead. Raise it for slow searches; lower it to give up sooner.

How much a single tool reply may carry for sub-agents (file reads, search results). Affects sub-agents only — the main chat is left exactly as upstream. Sub-agents have no terminal, so whatever gets cut off is lost to them and they must read on in several chunks. Raise it to finish big files in fewer steps; lower it if your sub-agent model has a small context window.

How many times a subagent may pick itself back up after being cut off mid-sentence, and also how many times an errored attempt is retried on the SAME model before falling back to the next one (a silent timeout switches immediately). Set to 0 to disable auto-retry entirely, so nothing continues without you asking.

One step = one model call (including the tools it wants to use that round). This cap only exists to stop a model from looping forever and burning money; hitting it is not a failure — the run is marked unfinished and picked up from where it stopped. Coding subagents automatically get 1.5x this number.

Runs as "one main model decides, the others hunt for blind spots": pin down the task and facts, then every model and the main model draft in parallel, then one model rebuts claim by claim, and finally the main model decides after seeing everything. Each step is one page you can flip through. Look-up only: never edits files or runs commands.
